speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Labour Movement was concerned that the COVID-19 pandemic had seemingly undone all the good workplace safety and health (WSH) practices nurtured over many years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The rush that many companies embarked on to clear the backlog of work had resulted in a spike in workplace accidents, injuries and fatalities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In my speech then, I had proposed five action areas to further improve WSH practices: (a) establish safe and easy-to-use Reporting channels; (b) partner the unions to enhance safety Inspections; (c) step up safety Gearing of our workers; (d) mandate Higher management's commitment to safety; and (e) leverage Technology to enhance workplace safety.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: These five areas make up the acronym "RIGHT".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In response, the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) instituted the Heightened Safety Period (HSP) in September 2022.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think we can all agree that the measures imposed under the HSP were unprecedented and tough but effective.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In his speech at the annual WSH Awards last month, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad provided an update on the workplace fatality rate.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Clearly, the additional WSH obligations and increased penalties against errant companies imposed by MOM as part of HSP had undoubtedly worked well in driving down workplace fatalities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Notable features of HSP included increased penalties for safety breaches, senior management having to account personally for serious safety lapses and barring errant companies from hiring foreign workers for up to three months.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Towards the end of HSP, the Labour Movement was concerned that workplace fatalities could rise if we were to exit HSP prematurely.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In May this year, I filed a Parliamentary Question asking if MOM could extend the HSP.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I was concerned that the strong safety culture imposed by company management during HSP did not have the necessary lead time to sink in and to take root.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lifting the HSP after just eight months could undo all our hard work.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: MOM eventually decided to lift the HSP from 1 June 2023 while retaining some of the HSP features, such as the enhanced penalties and requiring senior management to account personally for serious safety lapses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Unfortunately, my fears seem to be coming true.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I must add the caveat that this is not an official figure as the cases are a collation of inputs from our unions and associations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Every worker is a father or mother, son or daughter, brother or sister.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: They leave behind loved ones who mourn their passing, loved ones who have to deal with the sudden and unexpected loss of a key breadwinner of the family.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is why I have filed my second Adjournment Motion today on keeping our workplaces safe beyond the HSP.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In my first Adjournment Motion last year, I used the acronym "RIGHT" to encapsulate my five recommendations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My acronym today is "SAFE", which stands for: (a) Safety by design; (b) All workplaces to have a dedicated WSH professional; (c) Financial penalties to augment composition fines and stop work orders; and (d) Enforcement checks of unsafe workplace practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is a set of principles that prioritises the safety of workers when designing the worksite.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Today, MOM has in place the WSH (Design for Safety) Regulations that specify the duties of developers, contractors and designers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The scope of obligations should cover risks beyond just the construction phase.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: All workplaces, from blue-collar to white-collar jobs, should have a continuing obligation to design and provide a workplace that prioritises the safety of the workers. "Safety by design" considerations could include simple things such as proper lighting to prevent eye strain and even adopting anti-slip flooring materials to avoid slips, trips and falls.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Under our current law, the Workplace Safety and Health (Risk Management) Regulations state that employers are responsible for identifying safety and health hazards at workplaces and taking measures to eliminate or reduce the risks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: But, Sir, we must move away from this mental model of looking at risks and hazards as things to be managed away.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Instead, companies need to actively put safety at the forefront of designing their worksites and their offices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Companies that design workplaces for employees' safety will send a strong message to their employees that they care as an employer and will be rewarded with a healthier and more productive workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the US, the Occupational Safety and Health Law does place a continuing obligation on employers to provide a safe workplace, regardless of whether the sector is deemed to be high-risk.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that MOM could study relevant overseas jurisdictions and expand regulations to impose safety by design on all employers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Next, all workplaces need a dedicated WSH professional.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I am confident that mandating a WSH officer to review all aspects of safety in a company will help move the needle in making workplaces that much safer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Even if we cannot immediately move to mandate all workplaces to hire a dedicated WSH professional, we can and we should start by expanding the list of companies that are required to employ one.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Next, I propose that we should increase the financial penalties faced by companies in the event of a workplace fatality.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Currently, penalties for errant companies mostly involve composition fines and Stop Work Orders.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I propose for all Government agencies to include a WSH clause in every condition of their respective licences.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A construction company is at risk of being debarred under the Demerit Point System (DPS) should the company have frequent safety infringements.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The DPS concept should be expanded to all companies that are licensed in some shape or form by any Government agency.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This can be done by inserting WSH-related clauses into their licensing conditions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In line with this trend, workplace accidents at such worksites are also becoming commonplace.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Lastly, I urge MOM to further tighten enforcement of unsafe work practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Whenever there is a workplace accident or workplace fatality, it is very common to hear anecdotally that that particular unsafe work practice had been happening regularly, sometimes for months and sometimes even for years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While I note that MOM has been stepping up its enforcement operations, there is scope to do more because lives and limbs are at stake.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must step up enforcement checks more frequently to deter companies from cutting corners in workplace safety practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As I have mentioned numerous times in this House, we must make it easier for workers and members of the public to whistle-blow and flag unsafe workplace practices.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It should take no more than a snap of a picture and a short description of the egregious activity on a mobile application for anyone to flag out a potentially life-threatening and unsafe workplace practice.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: By doing what is safe and what is right, we can make our workplaces much safer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The Labour Movement stands ready to partner all our tripartite partners to keep our workplaces safe beyond the HSP.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To complement this year's national WSH campaign, NTUC will be launching our own WSH campaign later this week on Friday, with a focus on reporting without reprisal and on reporting without retribution.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers must feel safe to report any workplace safety concern to their management.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Workers can escalate any WSH matter to the unions if the company management fails to act on any safety reports.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A safe workplace must be a basic right for every worker.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A safe workplace must be a basic right for every worker.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I urge the Government and the industry to take workplace safety and health seriously, work closely with NTUC and do what is safe and right.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Together, we can help every worker return home from work safe and sound, every day.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Workplace safety and health (WSH) did not begin with the start of the Heightened Safety Period (HSP), and neither does it stop when the HSP ends.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Every worker deserves a safe and healthy working environment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will always strive for zero fatality as every fatality is one too many and every incident is preventable.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What this means is that we – the Government, employers and workers – must continue to strengthen our workplace safety culture and work environments to achieve this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Prior to the HSP, we faced a fatal injury rate of 1.6 in the first half of 2022 and this necessitated the heightened measures of HSP to stem the tide of incidents.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our progress one year on reflects the outcome from HSP, which ended on 31 May 2023.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I share the Member's concerns on the number of workplace fatalities since we exited the HSP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, we do need to recognise that there will be some month-to-month volatility in fatality numbers and assess the situation over a longer period.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Thus far, only four countries in the world have achieved a fatality rate of below 1.0 consistently.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Singapore ranked fifth based on our three-year average fatal injury rate, after the UK, the Netherlands, Sweden and Germany.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Other countries in Asia have not achieved this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, contrary to what the Member had shared, post-HSP, we have actually retained most of the broad-based and sectorial measures of the HSP, such as requiring chief executives to personally account for serious WSH lapses.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We also introduced a revised Demerit Points System to debar more errant construction companies from hiring foreign employees for a period of time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Following the HSP exit, the Multi-Agency Workplace Safety and Health Taskforce (MAST) introduced a set of Safe Accountability, Focus and Empowerment (SAFE) measures to instil greater WSH accountability at the sector, company and individual levels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MAST is progressively rolling out these SAFE measures and will continue to drive new measures.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Members can refer to the infographic in the handout on the various measures that we are implementing and have implemented.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope this assures Members that we hold ourselves to high standards and, even post-HSP, we will not let up on our efforts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have seen improvement in the construction sector in the first half of 2023.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In particular, fatal injuries for regular construction worksites have improved as our efforts have kept them vigilant.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: More targeted interventions are required for smaller-scale construction work, including renovations and facility management, which accounted for the majority of the fatal and major injuries in construction.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not so much the larger sites but all these renovations and maintenance work that have been causing us these issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are working with the relevant agencies to enhance the safety standards for such contractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MAST will also continue to strengthen WSH ownership in construction, such as by introducing more stringent safety requirements and a WSH bonus scheme for public project tenders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The expansion of the Demerit Points System to the manufacturing sector in October 2023 should deter WSH breaches and strengthen standards.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we are moving on from construction and now to manufacturing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Egregious companies will be temporarily debarred from hiring foreign workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I agree with the Member on the need to increase the financial penalties to deter WSH contraventions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: During HSP, we doubled the quantum of composition fines for WSH lapses and we have retained this measure.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Beyond composition fines and Stop Work Orders, the maximum penalty for WSH Act breaches for an individual is a fine of up to $200,000 and/or two years' imprisonment, while that for a company is a fine of up to $500,000.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the Member’s suggestion to expand the current WSH (Design for Safety) Regulations, I agree that "Design for Safety" is important.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is an upstream process to identify and reduce risks through good design at the conceptual and planning stages, such as incorporating safe access to maintenance in the building design.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Employers' duties to conduct risk management and take reasonable steps to eliminate or minimise risk serve as a safety net.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This ensures that employers continuously provide and maintain a safe and healthy work environment for their employees.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In doing so, they should already consider control measures, such as providing appropriate safety training and equipment, to reduce the risks.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Competent WSH officers who can manage WSH risks are essential to support better WSH outcomes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MAST is looking to strengthen the effectiveness of our WSH officers and their reporting lines to stakeholders so that they can carry out their duties better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the Member's suggestion to expand WSH officers to other higher-risk industries, we will need to assess the effectiveness of having WSH officers in such industries and the potential impact on workplace fatal and major injuries.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this is something that we will study.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Even so, what is more important is for corporate leadership to take charge and be accountable for workplace safety and health.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Corporate leaders have influence over resources and priorities that drive their organisations' safety culture.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM had earlier rolled out the Approved Code of Practice for Company Directors' WSH Duties to provide guidance on how they may fulfil their WSH obligations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is aligned with the Member's suggestion to have a disqualification framework or to extend WSH penalties from joint ventures to partnering companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Member suggested that MOM should tighten our WSH enforcement and make the reporting of unsafe workplace practices easier.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM has not wavered in our enforcement efforts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the contrary, we have intensified inspections to ensure that employers maintain a strong focus on safety.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is not just about the workers, but it is also about those around them, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The campaign called for employers to facilitate an internal reporting system for workers to report unsafe workplace practices to their supervisors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, SnapSAFE, as the Member suggested, is easy to use.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One just uploads a photo and keys in a brief description of the occurrence, and we will take it from there.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While we have exited HSP, rest assured that we will continue to pursue safe measures to build stronger workplace safety culture and ownership across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: All of us, from corporate leadership, industry associations, union leaders to workers, must continue to play our part to uplift workplace safety and health so that every worker can return home safely to their loved ones.
